Automatic effort and model, and a quota that limits how many agents run, not how well one runs. Every request runs at the effort its grade calls for (zetetic-genius) and the main tool loop steps down the ladder. A subagent runs on the model its Agent call names, else the one its agent definition pins (read from the definition file, since agent.spawn carries only the call's), else the one the DESIGN block of its prompt names, else, for an inheriting type nobody designed, the rung of the dispatch table (hooks/dispatch-table.ts) for its task's class: one haiku completion grades the spawn prompt (routine, planned, bugfix, analysis, critical; a review or not), and the table gives model and effort (no haiku rung; a review runs on opus when complex, else on sonnet). A classifier that gives no class decides nothing: the spawn inherits and a POLICY row says why. Its effort is the Agent call's, else the one its definition sets, else DESIGN's, else the table's; an inheriting type the call gave a model runs every step at the effort of the turn's grade (main's spawns on a graded turn; a fork, a workflow agent or a teammate is never rewritten). No pressure, quota or context changes a model or an effort the orchestrator designed. Each spawn's requested, definition and decided model, what ran, the effort decided for its steps, the table's class and a short reason for each are kept per session.
